title: What Is More Painful, a BBL or a Tummy Tuck?
meta_description: Neither is proven to hurt more: we found no study comparing them. How a BBL and a tummy tuck each feel, day by day, how long it lasts and when to call.
excerpt: We found no study that compares BBL and tummy tuck pain head to head, but medical sources describe each clearly. Where it hurts, the hardest days, how long pain medicine is needed and when you can work again.
quick_answer:
What is more painful, a BBL or a tummy tuck?

Neither is proven to hurt more: we found no study comparing them. After a tummy tuck with muscle repair, you use those muscles to stand, and The Aesthetic Society says discomfort eases to a nagging level by 5 to 7 days. After a BBL, most need pain medication for 4 to 5 days, a plastic surgeon interviewed by ASPS says.

sources.title: Tummy Tuck - Aftercare & Recovery

Call your surgeon immediately if you notice an increase in swelling, pain, redness, drainage, or bleeding in the surgical area, or if you develop fever, dizziness, nausea, or vomiting. Other red flags include shortness of breath, chest pains, and an unusual heartbeat.
Remember, you must not take aspirin or certain anti-inflammatory medications.
You won't feel like yourself for at least seven to ten days and you still shouldn't do any heavy lifting (such as picking up your children or baskets of laundry) for four to six weeks.
Recovery from a tummy tuck procedure occurs over a period of six months or more.
You will also need to wear a wide elastic compression garment to reduce swelling and provide support to the skin as it tightens.
The first few days after surgery, you should rest.
Plan to take about two weeks off from work, depending on the physical demands of your job.
You should be up and walking the day after surgery, but take it slow.
